chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Ibn Muskān from 'Abd al-Mu'min said:

I instructed a man to ask Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) on my behalf about a man who caught fish while they were alive, then took them out after some of them had died. He said: 'That which died, do not eat it, for it died in the medium in which it was alive.'
ai.seo_question: Is fish halal if it dies in the water before being caught?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the condition of *hayat* (life) in aquatic creatures, ruling that if a fish dies while still in the water, it is considered *maytah* (dead by natural causes) and thus non-halal. This establishes a distinct criterion from land animals, where slaughter is required, emphasizing that the state of death relative to the natural habitat determines permissibility in Shia fiqh.
